source_title: South Koreans Demand Changes to Call of Duty: MW4 Opening Sequence
source_excerpt:
South Koreans are calling for changes to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's opening sequence, as the game uses real footage from the Itaewon tragedy in 2022. Because of its premise, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has not been exempt from controversy, and now Activision has responded to concerns about its opening montage.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's main story begins when North Korea invades South Korea's Hajin City, sparking a large-scale war. To give players context of the conflict, the game's opening sequence features a montage of clips portraying the consequences, such as fabricated news reports of Russia joining the war. Although the events of the game are fictional, some South Korean players have noticed that a particular real-life video was used in Modern Warfare 4 and are demanding alterations.
South Koreans Disapprove of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Using Real Itaewon News Footage
As reported by South Korean SBS News , real news footage from the Itaewon crowd crush tragedy from Halloween 2022 has been spotted in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's campaign opening sequence. The clip in question shows an emergency responder performing CPR on a victim. Recently, the 10.29 Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association released a statement asking Activision to remove the video from Modern Warfare 4 entirely. The organization also described the use of the clip as "highly inappropriate and senseless" considering that many South Korean families and citizens still suffer from trauma. "If the game developer has even a minimum level of courtesy and empathy toward the victims, they should promptly take corrective measures," continues the statement, as translated by SBS.
The Korean Game Consumers Association also released a statement, arguing that Activision should properly apologize for using the Itaewon footage and release an update replacing the clip in Modern Warfare 4 's opening. On the other hand, the consumers' rights group emphasized that this controversy should not be used to demand censorship of the game's content. Activision later issued a response to South Koreans' concerns, acknowledging the inclusion of real-life news footage to convey the game's narrative. "There was absolutely no intention to reference or lightly treat any real tragic events, including the Itaewon tragedy," added the developer. Since its launch, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has received updates improving its gameplay, ranging from weapon buffs to the addition of wager matches. Whether the game will change its opening sequence in a later patch remains to be seen.
While it is not uncommon for a Call of Duty title to draw from real-life political tensions to fictionalize a war, Modern Warfare 4 's premise has particularly been criticized by some players for tapping into a real fear that South Koreans live with. Not all representatives of the nation disapprove of the game's story, though. One lawmaker advised the South Korean President to play Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , since it reflects on the country's readiness against a potential invasion.
In the first week since its release, Modern Warfare 4 received a very positive response from franchise fans. Activision has already teased what's to come for the game in the coming months. On November 6, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's Season 1 will drop three new multiplayer maps, including the Shoot House map from past Modern Warfare titles. Infected and Possession Modes are also launching on October 29 and 30.
